title: Add chapter on OOP (follow up to #36)
description:
Ok here is a rough first stab to get this going.

My sense is that I may have channeled the content from Adv-R a little too directly and included more detail than necessary, but it seems tricky to know where to draw the line between style and implementation, since some exposition is necessary to illustrate principles concretely. Hopefully you'll be able to give some feedback/suggestions on how to tackle this if my approach is too long-winded by comparison to previous chapters.

I suppose an important part of this is getting a better sense of who the intended audience is/isn't (can you clarify this for me?) in order to know what level of knowledge can be assumed, how much context is required, and thus how to scope things.

I also may just be focusing on the wrong things so far - so please feel free to give me an indication of what else should be covered either instead of or in addition to what's here.

title: A Primer on Code Documentation
description:
This PR builds on #21 and tries to extend the style guide with regard to code documentation. It is not thought to be complete yet, but should rather serve as a starting point for discussion around what conventions should be followed when documenting with `roxygen2`.

I started a review and added a few comparisons to base R. I know it's not the goal of this style guide to replicate R base style, but it can't hurt to have a reference I think, in particular if it's ambiguous what is *best practice*, we might just want to stick with base R convention.
